# Parley v0.1.27

This release adds local Linux container panes for Claude Code and Codex while
Parley's native macOS core and Ghostty continue to own the workbench and TTY.

## Container panes

- Choose Run in a container in the pane's permission review and check a locally
  installed image. The launch pins its exact image ID and local Unix-socket
  daemon. Parley does not build or download images.
- The container runs as the person's numeric user and group, with one writable
  project folder, its own relay endpoint, read-only protocol/shim files and a
  private named home volume. Host vendor credentials and the Docker socket are
  not mounted. The external daemon remains outside Parley's control.
- Sign in inside the container using the vendor's subscription flow. For
  Codex, choose Sign in with Device Code and complete it in your Mac browser.
- The Linux command shim supports pane identity, attributed messages,
  Ask/Answer, Delegate, context staging and returned files through the existing
  capability transport. Host opening is refused inside the container.
- A CONTAINER indicator identifies these panes. Process lists show the host
  Docker client. A reviewed command run still requests a new human Shell on
  the host, and its preview identifies the container source.

## Lifetime and recovery

- Closing the main window keeps containers running. Pane close, restart,
  Stop Everything and quit stop owned containers before ending their surfaces.
  Unconfirmed cleanup is reported and prevents that lifecycle action.
- Status Center's Health section lists creation receipts and offers Stop and
  Remove. Cleanup verifies the exact container ID, daemon and ownership marker;
  names and labels alone do not grant authority.
- Failed launch preparation can be removed without trapping its pane. Removing
  an old receipt cannot stop a replacement container or host session.
- Vendor login, configuration and saved conversations survive in the pane's
  private named volume. Delete Saved Vendor State removes an unused volume
  after separate confirmation. Ordinary Parley history clearing keeps it.

## Compatibility

OrbStack was exercised with real transport, TTY resize, Control-C and cleanup
checks. Mark verified Codex device sign-in, an interactive reply, bidirectional
Parley messages and pane restart. The tested image requires Codex's explicitly
selected legacy Landlock setting, which Codex warns is deprecated. Permission
bypass flags are refused; a working default sandbox is follow-up work.

Claude's signed-in permission flow, resumed instruction uptake, login across a
full app relaunch, total host-plus-VM idle cost, and other images/daemons remain
compatibility follow-ups. Linked worktrees, additional approved folders and
container team provisioning are currently refused. These limits are documented
without holding the reviewed implementation out of this greenfield release.

Agent protocol is now 29. Existing agent panes need a person-authorized restart
to receive the changed launch instructions; Parley never restarts them silently.

Unnotarized test beta: ad-hoc signed without the hardened runtime, not
notarized, no automatic updates. Install only from the expected GitLab
release after checking SHA256SUMS.
